title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context, from the previous page. Grothendieck is studying the Galois (or Grothendieck–Teichmüller type) action on the profinite fundamental groupoids of the modular towers. Several groups are in play:
- the profinite group of the Legendre line U_{0,3} = P^1 − {0,1,∞};
- the group of M'_{1,1}, the moduli of elliptic curves with a Jacobi (full level-2) structure;
- the group GL(2, Ẑ).
Passing from U_{0,3} to M'_{1,1} creates a sign ambiguity, because the automorphism −1 of every elliptic curve acts trivially on level-2 structures. Hence the stack of elliptic curves with full level-2 structure is not isomorphic to U_{0,3}: it is a μ_2-gerbe over it. On fundamental groups, π_1(M'_{1,1}) is a central extension of π_1(U_{0,3}) by {±1}. Elements u of Π̃_σ are therefore only defined modulo sign.

The question asked on the previous page: is there a canonical lift Π̃_σ → Ñ_{1,1}, i.e. a canonical way to remove this sign ambiguity? Over Q one replaces Π̃_σ by Π_{Q,σ}. This is the section of the arithmetic fundamental group attached to the special rational point σ = 1/2 of U_{0,3}. That point is fixed by the involution x ↦ 1 − x of S_3, which also fixes ∞.

This page answers with the 'yoga standard', i.e. the anabelian dictionary between sections and rational points (section-conjecture yoga), applied to the gerbe M'_{1,1} → U_{0,3}.
- Lifts of the section Γ_Q → π_1(U_{0,3}) at λ = 1/2 to π_1(M'_{1,1}) should correspond to rational points of the gerbe lying over λ = 1/2.
- Such points are elliptic curves over Q with full level-2 rigidification and Legendre parameter 1/2.
- These curves form a torsor under H^1(Q, ±1) = Hom(Γ_Q, {±1}) = Q*/Q*^2, the quadratic twists.
- Lifts of a section through a central extension by {±1} likewise form a torsor under Hom(Γ_Q, {±1}).
- The two indeterminacies match, which 'essentially proves' the yoga is correct here.

Grothendieck draws two consequences.
1. No lift is really privileged, even over Γ_{Q,T} (Galois group unramified outside a finite set T). Indeed Hom(Γ_{Q,T}, ±1) is still nontrivial; for example Q(i), Q(√2) and Q(√−2) are unramified outside 2.
2. Lifts over Γ_{Q,T} do exist, because such curves exist.

The next page names the simplest one: y^2 = x(x−1)(x−1/2). It has j = 1728 and CM by Z[i], with bad reduction only at 2. 'Voilà le choix fait': it supplies a normalized lift. He then leaves open the problem of writing this lift explicitly in a computational formula.
errors: Calling M'_{1,1,Q} ≃ U_{0,3,Q} an 'isomorphism' is loose. As stacks, the level-2 moduli is a μ_2-gerbe over U_{0,3}, not isomorphic to it. Grothendieck's sign discussion implicitly accounts for this, so this is a matter of wording rather than a mathematical error.
Calling H^1(Q, ±1) 'the set of quadratic extensions' omits the trivial class. This is harmless.

ideas.what: Lifts of the Galois section at a rational point through the central μ_2-extension π_1(M(2)) → π_1(U_{0,3}) correspond to rational points of the gerbe (elliptic curves with level-2 structure and λ = 1/2), up to the action of Hom(Γ_Q, ±1) (quadratic twists).
ideas.modern_name: Section-conjecture correspondence for gerbes / stacky curves; obstruction and torsor for lifting sections through central extensions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck's anabelian section conjecture (1983 letter to Faltings); the stacky/gerbe version was studied later (e.g. Bresciani and others, 2010s–2020s)
ideas.where_published: The section conjecture is in the 1983 letter to Faltings; the gerbe version on this page appears unpublished

ideas.what: Use of the CM curve y^2 = x(x−1)(x−1/2) (j = 1728) at the S_3-symmetric point λ = 1/2 to normalize the GL(2, Ẑ)-valued Galois/GT lift (sign normalization).
ideas.modern_name: Normalization of the Galois action on π_1(M_{1,1}) / once-punctured elliptic curves via tangential or CM base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nakamura; Hain–Matsumoto (explicit Galois actions on π_1(M_{1,1}) and on elliptic fundamental groups, 1990s–2000s)

ideas.what: The sign ambiguity has no canonical resolution even over Γ_{Q,T}, because Hom(Γ_{Q,T}, ±1) is nontrivial.
ideas.modern_name: Non-canonicity of lifts / quadratic twist ambiguity

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes normalizing the lift of the Galois (GT-type) action from U_{0,3} to M_{1,1}[2] ⊂ GL(2, Ẑ) by the CM elliptic curve with λ = 1/2 (j = 1728). He wants an explicit 'formulaire calculatoire' for the resulting sign/character, but leaves this undone.
missed.quote: Qu'il y ait de tels relèvements (sur Γ_{Q,T}), provient du fait qu'il y a bel et bien des courbes elliptiques répondant à la question
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Explicit formulas for the Galois action on π_1(M_{1,1}) and on elliptic braid groups (Nakamura, Hain–Matsumoto, Enriquez's elliptic associators) usually use the Tate-curve tangential base point at ∞. A normalization at the j = 1728 CM point compatible with the S_3-symmetric point σ is a natural but less-explored choice. It could give a cleaner comparison between genus-0 GT data and the elliptic/GL_2 data.

missed.claim: The section-conjecture yoga is applied to a gerbe (stack) rather than a scheme. Lifting a section through a central μ_2-extension corresponds to choosing a twisted form, with torsor H^1(Q, μ_2).
missed.quote: les relèvements en question devraient correspondre aux courbes elliptiques sur Q, munies d'une rigidification de Jacobi d'échelon 2
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This anticipates the stacky section conjecture (sections of algebraic stacks/gerbes), which only received systematic treatment much later. It is a minor but early instance.

deep.surprise_reason: The argument is a short, correct and fairly natural application of the anabelian yoga to the μ_2-gerbe M(2) → P^1 − {0,1,∞}. Its early stacky/section-conjecture flavour and the concrete CM normalization at λ = 1/2 are mildly interesting, but specialists would find it unsurprising.
transcription_corrections: Line 4: there is a struck-out symbol before M'_{1,1,Q}; the prime on M is visible.
Line 8: the parenthetical is hard to read. It looks like '(c'est un ens.[?] d'ext. quadratiques de Q)' rather than 'c'est aussi l'ensemble des ext.'; the meaning is the same.
The insertion '(sur Π_{Q,T})' above 'relèvements' looks like Π or Γ in the image; context suggests Γ_{Q,T}.
